visuals.heading: Each Path Actually Leads

items.text: An MSCS deepens your technical skill and usually opens a faster route into strong-paying engineering roles abroad, at a lower total cost than an MBA abroad.

blocks.heading: Staying Technical Protects the Specific Skill

items.text: Staying technical protects the specific skill the market is already paying you for, rather than trading it for a broader but less proven one.
Most MSCS programmes are built around campus recruiting pipelines into product and tech companies.
Senior and staff-level engineering roles, applied research positions, and technical leadership tracks can match or exceed general-management pay without requiring you to leave hands-on work.

blocks.heading: Honest Case for Pivoting to Business

items.text: If a few years into your engineering job the parts you found most engaging were prioritization calls, stakeholder conversations, or business strategy, that is real evidence, not a guess.
Roles like management consulting, investment banking, and many product leadership tracks at large companies recruit specifically through MBA campus pipelines.

If your longer-term plan involves running a business, leading a large team, or making resource-allocation decisions across functions, the broader exposure an MBA gives you (finance, operations, marketing, strategy) can matter more than staying narrowly technical, especially once you already have solid engineering fundamentals to build on.
Burnout from a tough engineering job is a reason to look at your workload, manager, or team, not automatic proof that you want a career in business.
An MSCS is a strong move if you want to go deeper technically.

Most strong MBA programmes expect 2-5 years of real work experience, and admissions committees can tell the difference between a candidate with genuine leadership stories and one padding a resume early.

A top Indian MBA (IIM-tier) runs roughly ₹17-27.5 lakh for the full programme; an MBA abroad typically runs ₹80 lakh to ₹2.5 crore once tuition, insurance, and relocation are included
GRE (increasingly optional at many US programmes), strong CS fundamentals, and often a research or project-heavy application
GMAT or GRE, plus work-experience essays, references, and often an interview round that weighs leadership signals over test scores alone
Some funded research assistantships exist, mostly at PhD-track-adjacent labs; most MSCS students self-fund through education loans
Merit scholarships exist at a handful of top schools, but most Indian MBA abroad applicants still fund the bulk of the cost through loans
